report.verdict: The move from corporate FP&A to Marketing Operations Coordinator is a significant change in track. Your finance work is substantial, but I’d pass for this role because the resume doesn’t show marketing campaigns or the required HubSpot work.
write_up: Tallgrass is looking for marketing operations work, while your resume tells a finance story: branch profitability at Carolina Regional Bank followed by corporate FP&A at Piedmont Building Supply. For financial analyst roles, I’d move this forward with a few questions. For this posting, the change in track is the main obstacle.

The headcount model is your best model for the rest of the resume: it names Adaptive Planning and tells me what you replaced. Your experience is easy to follow, and it comes before education. The savings, forecasting and efficiency figures are worth attention, but a recruiter still needs to know what you did to produce them.

Let’s start with the Piedmont savings line, then add the work behind the forecasting and efficiency figures. For Tallgrass, include any relevant marketing operations work you can substantiate, rather than trying to make finance reporting stand in for campaign work.

cards.cannot_tell: The savings figure gets attention, but I can’t tell where you found it or what analysis you did. That matters for an FP&A role.
cards.question: Where did you find the savings, and what analysis did you do?

cards.cannot_tell: The improvement is useful, but the forecast and your approach are unnamed. A recruiter can’t tell which part of forecasting was yours.
cards.question: Which forecast improved, and what did you change?

cards.line: Rebuilt the headcount model in Adaptive Planning, replacing three disconnected spreadsheets
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives the recruiter a concrete deliverable, the tool and the previous setup in one line.
I can see the reported improvement, but not which reporting process changed or what you did to it.
cards.question: Which reporting process changed, and what did you do to improve it?

cards.cannot_tell: This names the area but leaves your contribution open. Which tasks did you automate, and what did you use?
cards.question: Which month-end tasks did you automate, and what tool did you use?

fit.why: Your headline and both roles center on financial analysis, reporting and forecasting.
fit.level: mid-level, current corporate FP&A role and prior financial analyst role
fit.note: Your reporting and analysis work gives you a foundation for the measurement side of marketing operations. The Tallgrass role is hybrid in Columbus, OH; your resume lists Charlotte, NC.

posting.summary: Marketing operations role focused on B2B campaigns, HubSpot and Salesforce, campaign reporting, and event support.
missing: 2+ years in marketing for a B2B company
Hands-on HubSpot experience: workflows, lists, email and reporting
Google Analytics 4 and building simple reports
record of running campaigns on deadline
